skill.name: blather-game-night-host
skill.description: Plan a Blather game night for two to six human players. Produce a correct turn schedule, a usable invitation, a short teaching script and a recap checklist from the host's inputs.
skill.summary: Prepare Blather turn schedules, invitations, teaching scripts, and host checklists for two to six human players.
skill.author: cnvxstudio

security_audit.summary: Both URL findings are false positives: they identify the game and its demo, not network operations or data transfers. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, or unauthorized actions; the instructions explicitly limit the skill to planning.

static_findings.snippet: - Blather is an independent English browser word party game: https://blatherround.com/ .
- The demo at https://blatherround.com/demo shows one prepared example; it is not a full solo game o

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md:14 identifies the game's public website as a product reference, without directing requests or transmitting information. The access limits explicitly state that network access is unnecessary.
SKILL.md:19 references the public demo to clarify its limited functionality, without directing network calls or data submission. The skill explicitly excludes browser and network requirements.

content.value_statement: Hosting a Blather game requires a clear turn schedule, invitation, and rules explanation. This skill prepares those materials from your group size, rounds, and gathering format.
actual_capabilities: Calculate total describing turns for two to six participants and one to five rounds.
Create a turn table giving each participant one describing turn per round.
Draft invitations using a supplied room invitation or explain that the host will provide it later.
Write a three-sentence rules script covering clues, guesses, turn-taking, and the applicable scoring format.
Prepare host checklists for joining, remote voice coordination, round readiness, and reviewing a real clue sequence.
Offer three recap questions about actual clues, surprising guesses, and interest in another game.
limitations: Does not create rooms, send invitations, control live games, or act as an AI player.
Plans individual rooms for two to six humans; larger gatherings require separate groups.
Does not verify live website behavior, undocumented features, point formulas, or guaranteed finish times.
Does not access player records, invent results, export clips, or publish social posts.

use_cases.title: Prepare a first gathering
use_cases.description: Create a turn schedule, invitation draft, and short teaching script for friends meeting in person.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a remote game
use_cases.description: Prepare a remote host checklist with voice-call coordination and an invitation using an existing room link.

use_cases.title: Split a larger gathering
use_cases.description: Plan separate groups within the six-player room limit and prepare distinct turn schedules for each group.

prompt_templates.title: Start a simple plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an in-person Blather night for four people, including me, with two rounds. We have not created a room yet.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a complete basic plan without a room invitation.

prompt_templates.title: Personalize the invitation
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan three rounds for these participants, including me: [names]. We will meet [in person or remotely]. Use this existing room invitation: [invitation].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: adapt the plan to participant names and an existing invitation.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a remote pair
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a remote Blather plan for two humans and five rounds. Include a turn table, cooperative-format teaching script, voice-call checklist, and recap questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: coordinate remote play with the two-player cooperative format.

prompt_templates.title: Organize separate groups
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan Blather for ten humans in two separate groups of five, with two rounds each. Use planning labels and draft pre-invitations without room links.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage a larger gathering without exceeding room capacity.

output_examples.input: Prepare the schedule and rules for two people playing two rounds. No names are available.
output: Group: two humans, two rounds, four describing turns, with a shared cooperative score.
Player A and Player B are planning labels, not confirmed participant names.
Round 1: Player A, then Player B. Round 2: Player A, then Player B.
The describer builds clues from limited word tiles. Other players type guesses, which may be reused in later clues. Everyone describes once per round, and two players share a cooperative score.

output_examples.input: Draft an invitation and recap questions for four remote players, including the host, playing one round. The room is not created.
output: Join our remote Blather game for four people and one round. The host will send the room link after creating it.
Please coordinate the voice call with the host before the game.
Which actual clue helped the group most?
Would the group like another game?

best_practices: Provide the participant count including the host, round count, gathering format, and any existing room invitation.
Use supplied names or clearly labeled planning names, and verify one describing turn per participant per round.
Base recaps on actual play and review names and guesses before any manual clip export.
anti_patterns: Requesting invented room links, participant attendance, scores, or memorable moments.
Treating the prepared demo as a full solo game or an AI opponent.
Expecting automatic room creation, invitation delivery, clip export, or social publication.

faq.question: How many people can play in one room?
faq.answer: The skill documents two to six human participants, including the host. Larger gatherings need separate groups.

faq.question: How does the skill calculate turns?
faq.answer: Each participant describes once per round. Total describing turns equal the participant count multiplied by the round count.

faq.question: Can it create a room or send invitations?
faq.answer: No. It drafts planning materials and can include a room invitation you provide. You create the room and send messages yourself.

faq.question: What happens when I have no room link?
faq.answer: It writes a pre-invitation stating that the host will send the room link after creating it. It does not invent links or codes.

faq.question: Does it play the game or generate answers?
faq.answer: No. It is a planning assistant, not an AI player or answer generator. The referenced demo is only one prepared example.

faq.question: Does this skill need credentials or network access?
faq.answer: No. Planning uses supplied inputs and documented facts without credentials, browser access, or external APIs. Actual multiplayer play happens separately.
